subject: shinyapps.io: Common or unique working directory for each instance of an app?

messages.author: a08511b61d1423a7
messages.subject: shinyapps.io: Common or unique working directory for each instance of an app?
parts:
My app exports files into the working directory during runtime which is read back in later and plotted. I noticed that when the same app is used simultaneously from say two tabs in a browser but with different input files. The output plots conflict.
So, when the same app on shinyapps.io is started in a multiple browser/tabs, does each instance run in the same directory or does each instance have its own working directory?

For the same issue on a shiny-server environment, I created a new directory based on time each time the app starts and all outputs are generated in that directory. But that doesn't seem to work for shinyapps.io.
Thanks.

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io: Common or unique working directory for each instance of an app?
parts:
Yes. Each R process (worker) runs in the same directory on the server. A worker process can handle more then one session (connection). Additionally your application will automatically start more then one worker process if its needed (depending on the application settings and the number of connections). If two sessions (connections) need isolation to write files, you should create a temp directory.

If you have more then one instance of the application (e.g. more then one server), all their workers will also be running in the same directory.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io: new directories per connection
parts:
Thanks. I am trying to create new directories each time a connection is made to the app or when a new set of files is uploaded. Do you know any approach to creating new directory for each connection to the app. Here are some of my attempts below:

TRY1

#server.R
#Create new directory and change wd
currentwd <- getwd()
newwd <- paste0(currentwd,"/",format(Sys.time(),"%Y%m%d%H%M%S"))
dir.create(newwd)
setwd(newwd)


shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  #something here
  #export some files to current directory.
}

Above works locally. Each time the app is started a new directory is created. But this does not work in a server environment. The first time the app is started, a new directory is created. All new connections (opening the app again in new tabs/browser/computer etc) does not create a new directory. 

Then I thought that might be because the new dir block is not inside shinyServer. Fiddling around for a bit, I came up with below:

TRY 2
#server.R
cwd <- getwd()

#function
fn_dir <- function(currentwd)
{
newwd <- paste0(currentwd,"/",format(Sys.time(),"%Y%m%d%H%M%S"))
dir.create(newwd)
setwd(newwd)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  store <- reactiveValues(currentwd=cwd)

  fn_upload({
  inputdata <- input$files
  fn_dir(store$currentwd)
  })

  #export some files to current directory.
}

In this case, new directory is not created when the app is started. When files are uploaded, `fn_upload()` is run which creates a new directory. The directory is created as expected, but all files are still exported inside the first created directory.
The directories are not changed anywhere else in the app.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io: new directories per connection
parts:
Roy, 
I am not a shiny expert, but your first try is not going to work because the creation of the directory will happen once and only once as you point out.  In Try 2, you are setting the working directory for the entire R process every time, which would make any other session that starts set the directory to original directory, what I think you want to do is to be writing out to the path of the directory instead.  My bet is that this would be easier to debug if you could put together a simple version of your application and I suspect that the shiny-discuss list folk would be able to point out where the problem lies.

-Tareef

parts:
Apologies! Here is a working example now.

#ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  headerPanel("New directory issue"),
  wellPanel(
  helpText("I would like a new directory to be created each time a new connection is made to the app OR anytime new files are uploaded."),
  helpText("This app uploads one text file, creates a new directory, extracts first 5 lines and exports a text file with the contents."),
  helpText("Upload one text file with minimum 5 lines of content."),
  fileInput('upload', label=h4('Upload file(s):'), multiple=FALSE)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    tags$h3("Str of uploaded content"),
    verbatimTextOutput('display')
  )
))


#server.R

#Get current wd and print
currwd <- getwd()

#FUNCTION - new directory
fn_dir <- function(currwd=NULL)
{
  if(is.null(currwd)) stop("Argument 'currwd' is empty.\n")

  #Create new working directory
  newwd <- paste0(currwd,"/",format(Sys.time(),"%Y%m%d%H%M%S"))
  dir.create(newwd)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  #REACTIVE - store
  store <- reactiveValues(currwd = currwd)
 
  #REACTIVE - complete input
  fn_getfilenames <- reactive({
    inputdata <- input$upload
   
    if (!is.null(inputdata))
    {
      print(paste0("Start dir: ",store$currwd))
      fn_dir(store$currwd)
      print(paste0("New dir: ",getwd()))
      return(inputdata)
    }else{
      return(NULL)
    }
  })
 
  #OUTPUT
  output$display <- renderPrint({
    if (is.null(fn_getfilenames())) return(NULL)
   
    inputdata <- fn_getfilenames()
   
    #some stuff to export to working directory
    rcontent <- as.vector(scan(file = inputdata$datapath,what = "text",n = 10))
    write(x = rcontent, file = paste0(inputdata$name,"-test.txt"))
       
    return(str(inputdata))
  })
})

I am also curious as to why the print statements appear in the str() output.
Thanks.

Hi Roy,
I suspect that you will have the best luck by posting your example on the shiny-discuss list since I am not really an R expert, but I took a look at the working code you sent and found that it doesn't write the file in the subdirectory when I run it locally on my machine.  

I took the liberty of changing your server.R code a bit so that it does two key changes, you will see is that I am storing the new directory name that was created, and then using that when it comes time to writing it out to disk.

Again, these types of questions are more of a question about shiny development and less to do with shinyapps.io.  
HTH

Tareef

#server.R

#Get current wd and print
currwd <- getwd()

#FUNCTION - new directory
fn_dir <- function(currwd=NULL)
{
  if(is.null(currwd)) stop("Argument 'currwd' is empty.\n")
  
  #Create new working directory

newwd <- paste0(currwd,"/",format(Sys.time(),"%Y%m%d%H%M%S"))
  dir.create(newwd)
  newwd

}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  #REACTIVE - store
  store <- reactiveValues(currwd = currwd)
  
  #REACTIVE - complete input
  fn_getfilenames <- reactive({
    inputdata <- input$upload
    
    if (!is.null(inputdata))
    {
store$newwd <- fn_dir(store$currwd)

return(inputdata)
    }else{
      return(NULL)
    }
  })
  
  #OUTPUT
  output$display <- renderPrint({
    if (is.null(fn_getfilenames())) return(NULL)
    
    inputdata <- fn_getfilenames()
    
    #some stuff to export to working directory
    
    rcontent <- as.vector(scan(file = inputdata$datapath,what = "text",n = 10))

full_file_path <- file.path(store$newwd,inputdata$name)
    write(x = rcontent, file = paste0(full_file_path,"-test.txt"))
    
    return(str(inputdata))
  })
})
